text: Cultist-style enemies become more dangerous the longer the fight lasts. Early focused damage is valuable when the current hand can still keep HP risk acceptable.
Slime fights often punish scattered damage. Focus a practical kill or split threshold instead of spreading low damage across several enemies.
Chomper-style fights reward efficient damage while respecting incoming attacks. If a kill is not close, block or mitigation can preserve HP without losing too much tempo.
Against multiple small enemies, removing one attacker can reduce future incoming damage more than spreading damage evenly.
BASH is mainly a Vulnerable setup and damage amplifier. It is strongest when Vulnerable enables meaningful follow-up damage this turn or next turn.
Block cards buy HP when damage cannot be prevented by lethal or strong debuff timing. Small HP loss can be acceptable if it accelerates a decisive kill.
Cheap draw attacks can be better than overkill when they kill a low-HP enemy and keep options open for the rest of the turn.
Forgotten Ritual is higher value after a card has been Exhausted this turn. Consider its timing before spending the last energy.
BURNING_BLOOD heals after combat, so the planner can treat some HP as a resource when the line speeds up the fight and avoids large future damage.
With HAND_DRILL, breaking enemy Block can create a Vulnerable payoff window. The planner should look for block-break timing before the largest follow-up attack.
FORTIFIER is a defensive potion whose value depends on existing Block. It is most relevant when it prevents major HP loss or death after some Block is already available.
Boss fights justify spending stronger resources earlier than normal fights when the resource prevents a large HP swing or unlocks a decisive damage window.
BASH costs 2 and applies Vulnerable after dealing damage, so its value depends on whether the debuff enables later Attack damage, not just its immediate hit.
Vulnerable increases damage from Attacks and usually decays at end of turn. Planner hints should prefer Attack follow-up windows and avoid assuming non-Attack HP loss benefits.

STS2 Cultists buff on their first turn and then attack repeatedly. Damp Cultist has higher Ritual scaling while Calcified Cultist starts with stronger attack pressure, so focus should depend on current kill reach and incoming damage.

Soul Fysh follows a predictable cycle with Beckon status pressure, direct attacks, a Fade turn, and a later Vulnerable attack. Planner hints should time damage around Fade and keep defense ready for the fixed attack turns.

The Insatiable opens by adding Sandpit/Frantic Escape pressure, then cycles multi-hit damage, a large bite, and Strength gain. Planner hints should avoid slow lines that let Strength scaling outpace defense.

STS2 bosses appear after a Rest Site and have larger HP pools plus special gimmicks. Planner hints can be more willing to spend potions or setup resources when they prevent a major boss-pattern swing.

Hand Drill style Vulnerable is triggered by actually breaking enemy Block; removing Block without breaking it may not create the same payoff. Planner hints should look for real block-break attacks before payoff Attacks.
Burning Blood is Ironclad's starter relic in STS2. The planner may value tempo lines that take modest HP loss, but only when they reduce later risk enough to justify relying on post-combat healing.
